Spain Technology Ventures

EDA and project fit | Egyptian Startup Intelligence System | 23 October 2026

Keep this dataset for a small, reproducible ML experiment and data-quality training. It does not support a dependable Egyptian startup risk score or our cash-flow simulation. The usable label is survival in 2014 among Spanish ventures that had already reached the 2009 survey.

The original SAV file was downloaded again and checked against Zenodo's published MD5 checksum. This report uses the actual records and their SPSS metadata, not the earlier shortlist counts alone. Source: Zenodo record and original download.

Source · Target · Quality · Insights · ML check · Project questions · Team actions

1. What was collected

There are 175 rows and 47 original fields, with one reported venture per row. The public file has no company name or stable company identifier. A generated source_row preserves row lineage only and is never a model input. Exact duplicate rows: 0; exact duplicate survey profiles: 0; constant fields: 0. Without identifiers, this does not independently prove that all entities are distinct.

DateMeaning
2009Founder-manager questionnaire, referring to resources at or near inception and performance through 2008.
2008 and 2014Years attached to the financial measurements; the binary survival outcome refers to 2014.
2016Researchers retrieved financial and survival information from SABI.
2024Dataset publication year. It is not the observation year.

The source describes independent Spanish technology ventures, fewer than 250 employees and up to eight years old at recruitment. The file contains observations that need reconciliation with those criteria. The authors' institutional repository confirms the study design and the dataset's CC BY 4.0 license. Attribution must accompany reuse.

Field groups: knowledge-source scores (7), partner access (2), training and experience (6), innovation (4), strategy and perceived performance (10), firm/founder descriptors (8), survival (1), internationalization (1), and financial measures for two years (8). Score values are mostly 1-7, with training/experience at 1-5. They are ordinal responses, not years of experience, actual customer counts, growth percentages or investment amounts. The exact response anchors are not included in the SAV labels and remain to be obtained.

2. Target and imbalance

Survival_2014 = 1 means survived; 0 means did not survive. For evaluation, non_survival_2014 = 1 - Survival_2014, so the minority event is the positive class. The dataset does not provide a documented closure date, reason or bankruptcy event. The 25 unknown outcomes are kept for descriptive auditing and excluded from supervised fitting; they are not assigned invented labels.

status count percent_all
Survived in 2014 110 62.857
Did not survive in 2014 40 22.857
Outcome unknown 25 14.286

Among the 150 known outcomes, non-survival is 26.7%, survival is 73.3%, and the majority/minority ratio is 2.75:1. This is manageable class imbalance; the more serious constraint is only 40 minority examples. Five-fold validation leaves 8 non-survivors per validation fold. One missed event therefore changes fold recall by 12.5 percentage points.

A model that always predicts survival gets 73.3% accuracy while detecting no non-survivors. Report average precision (AP), minority recall/precision/F1, balanced accuracy and ROC-AUC. AP's prevalence baseline is 0.267. The Wilson 95% interval for the observed minority proportion is 20.2%-34.3%; it does not establish a national failure rate. If all 25 missing outcomes were survivors or non-survivors, the full-file non-survival proportion would range from 22.9% to 37.1%. These are extreme-case bounds, not predictions.

Class weights were used inside training. No SMOTE or artificial rows were added. If resampling is tried later, it belongs inside training folds only. Standard SMOTE also needs care with ordinal and categorical fields. Neither weighting nor oversampling adds new real companies.

3. Cleaning, missingness and leakage

9999 is a missing-value code. The SPSS file explicitly declares it, including the text version for Sector. The cleaning step replaced 242 actual coded cells with missing values using metadata, then preserved system-missing values. The result has 1,022 missing cells (12.43% of the 8,225 original cells). The raw SAV and raw-value export are retained unchanged.

Each 2008 financial field is missing in 64/175 rows (36.6%). Within known labels, those fields are missing in 20/40 non-survivors (50%) and 19/110 survivors (17.3%). All 25 unknown-outcome rows lack all four 2008 financial fields. This pattern is inconsistent with a simple assumption that missing records are unrelated to outcomes. It does not identify the exact missing-data mechanism.

Blind complete-case deletion destroys the target. Keeping only rows complete across every column leaves 34 records, all survivors. Keeping the nine core predictors and a known label retains 142 complete records; fold-local imputation lets the exploratory model retain all 150 labeled records.

selection remaining_rows non_survived survived
All 47 columns 34 0 34
Survey fields plus label 138 38 100
Core 9 plus label 142 38 104
2008 financial fields plus label 111 20 91

Exclude all five non-target 2014 fields. They are future information for an earlier prediction. Their missingness indicators are also future information. The 2008 financial values need a separate decision: the year is earlier, but the records were extracted in 2016, and their availability strongly follows eventual outcomes. We therefore keep them out of the primary survey baseline and use them only for an explicitly limited sensitivity check. Imputation cannot establish that a field was available at the original decision time.

Other quality issues

  • Firm age: values range from 4 to 350; the unit is not specified. A months interpretation is plausible but unverified. Under that assumption, 42 rows exceed 96 months. Do not silently divide by 12 or discard those rows. Firm age is excluded from the baseline pending clarification.
  • Employees: median 4, range 0-1,100 among 165 observed values. Two values, 300 and 1,100, conflict with the stated fewer-than-250 selection rule unless timing or another explanation resolves it. There are 19 zero-employee companies; these are not automatically invalid. Outliers are flagged, retained in raw data and checked in a sensitivity experiment.
  • Sector: 97 original strings become 88 after case, accent and whitespace normalization. Of those 88 categories, 69 occur once. Ten values are missing. A reviewed taxonomy is needed before sector-level inference or categorical modeling. UTF-8 source accents are intact; normalization is not a claim of semantic equivalence.
  • Financial values: profits may legitimately be negative; extreme profitability values need review. Currency, scale and precise accounting definitions are not resolved by the labels. No currency conversion or revenue-growth label was invented.
  • Redundant fields: where both are observed, the founding-team flag agrees with whether founder count exceeds one. The baseline keeps count alone.
  • Coverage: one country and one historical recruitment cohort. Founders who did not reach the 2009 survey are not represented. The file has 146 male and 20 female respondents, with 9 missing; such small, unbalanced subgroups cannot justify demographic conclusions. Gender and entrepreneur age are descriptive only in this experiment.
  • Internationalization: source categories 1 and 3 both describe internationalization; 69.7% of values are missing. Resolve the ambiguous coding before using it as a separate target.

4. What the exploratory comparisons show

Survivors have a median of 5 employees versus 2 among non-survivors. Same-sector experience scores have medians 3 versus 2. These are useful hypotheses to test with larger data; they do not show that hiring or experience causes survival. The employee comparison has an unadjusted p-value of 0.033 but a survey-family BH-adjusted q-value of 0.371. No individual survey feature passes q < 0.05 in the exploratory numeric screening.

Pioneers have an observed non-survival proportion of 32.6% (14/43), versus 24.5% (26/106) for followers. Fisher's exact p-value is 0.317 and the intervals overlap widely. This is not sufficient evidence to recommend one technology strategy over the other. Subgroup comparisons are unadjusted for confounding.

Foreign-sales and foreign-market-expansion scores have Spearman correlation 0.769; local-sales-growth and market-share scores have correlation 0.692. Some questionnaire items carry overlapping information. These are self-reported scores, not measured growth rates. Use regularization and avoid treating 32 correlated inputs as 32 independent pieces of evidence.

5. A small predictive-signal check

We tested three fixed model families plus a simple equal-weight probability ensemble and a prevalence baseline. All use the same nine business features, picked for their meaning rather than their univariate ranking: founder count, employees, technology strategy, access to investment and technology partners, sector and management experience scores, customer dialogue, and R&D emphasis.

Protocol: 5 stratified folds, repeated with 10 seeds (42-51). Each company is predicted once per repeat by a model that did not train on it. Median imputation and logistic-regression scaling fit only on the training fold. Employee counts receive a fixed log(1+x) transform. Survey scores are treated as ordered numeric inputs, an approximation that assumes useful numeric spacing. No feature selection, hyperparameter search, threshold tuning or synthetic data was used. The classification threshold stays at 0.5. The ensemble averages the three held-out predictions. This is internal exploratory cross-validation, not an independent final test or an Egyptian validation.

Logistic regression uses C=0.3 and balanced class weights. Random forest uses 150 trees, maximum depth 3 and at least 8 rows per leaf. Histogram gradient boosting uses 80 iterations, at most 5 leaves, at least 12 rows per leaf and L2 regularization 5. These settings are reproducible trial choices, not tuned optima.

Model ROC-AUC AP (non-survival) Balanced accuracy Precision Recall F1 Brier (lower is better)
Prevalence baseline 0.500 0.267 0.500 0.000 0.000 0.000 0.196
Logistic regression 0.602 0.377 0.587 0.343 0.573 0.429 0.241
Random forest 0.524 0.286 0.523 0.290 0.440 0.349 0.244
Gradient boosting 0.542 0.291 0.533 0.302 0.417 0.350 0.251
Equal-weight ensemble 0.565 0.312 0.557 0.326 0.465 0.383 0.239

The core logistic baseline is the strongest of these trials, with mean ROC-AUC 0.602 and AP 0.377. Its minority recall is 57.3%, but precision is only 34.3% at the fixed threshold. The ensemble's ROC-AUC is 0.565; averaging these models did not improve the logistic baseline. This does not rule out every other model, but it gives no basis for a reliable deployed risk score.

For the first OOF partition, logistic regression detects 21/40 non-survivors, misses 19 and falsely flags 42 survivors. A fixed logistic-regression label-permutation check with 199 permutations gives p=0.090 for mean fold ROC-AUC. It does not clear a conventional 0.05 threshold. This is a limited signal check, not proof that no relationship exists.

Scores are not calibrated risk probabilities. Core-model Brier scores are worse than the constant prevalence baseline (0.196). Class weighting shifts the effective class distribution. Calibration needs its own validation and more observations; this report does not convert these scores into personal risk advice.

Sensitivity checks and the misleading shortcut

Using all 32 survey features gives logistic regression an average ROC-AUC of 0.635 over five partitions, still modest and not a separately confirmed result. Removing the influence of the employee values that conflict with recruitment criteria barely changes the core result. Adding 2008 financial values does not improve this trial.

More tellingly, using only the missingness of the 2014 financial fields gives an apparent ROC-AUC of 0.776. This is an intentionally invalid leakage demonstration: it uses information collected at the outcome year. It must never be presented as successful forecasting. Even 2008 financial missingness alone gives about 0.617; this reinforces the need to audit the 2016 retrieval process and the availability of fields at decision time.

6. Which project questions can this source answer?

Project question Use Reason
Which early firm and founder characteristics are associated with survival by 2014? Yes, exploratory 150 labeled Spanish ventures. Associations are uncertain and not causal.
Can early survey responses distinguish survivors from non-survivors in this cohort? Small ML experiment Evaluate a historical binary classifier using pre-outcome fields; current baseline signal is weak.
How much does the choice of model or ensemble help? Yes, methodological Same target, same folds and feature set. The equal-weight ensemble did not improve on logistic regression.
What is an Egyptian startup's failure probability in the next 12 or 24 months? No Different country, historical cohort, no such horizon labels and no local validation.
When will a startup close? What is its one-, two- or five-year survival curve? No No closure dates, event durations or individual last-observation dates.
What happens to cash runway if expenses fall by 20%? No direct support No cash balance, monthly receipts/payments, burn or runway. Use founder inputs and cash-flow calculations.
How would inflation or an exchange-rate shock affect this company? No direct support No exposure data or varied country-year panel from which to learn the relationship.
Would adding a co-founder or spending more on R&D cause survival to improve? No causal answer Observational survey associations do not identify interventions; no measured R&D spending is provided.
Can we study financial changes between 2008 and 2014? Limited descriptive use 71 paired operating-income observations; selected subset, unknown units, six-year interval. Not monthly or 12-month growth.
Can the dataset or related papers support RAG? Yes, with a narrow scope Use the source description and research as historical Spanish evidence, with dates and limitations; not Egyptian market facts.

The defensible modeling question is: “Among ventures represented in this Spanish survey, do early recorded business characteristics help distinguish survival from non-survival by 2014?” The outcome is a fixed calendar-year status, about five years after recruitment, not a rolling five-year prediction from each company's birth and not a 24-month failure target.

For the product, keep founder-entered cash, receipts, expenses and scenario assumptions in a separate cash-flow calculator. No field in this source gives a direct coefficient for “cut expenses 20%” or “increase R&D spending.” A model explanation describes associations learned from these records; it cannot estimate the effect of taking such an action.

7. What the team should do next

  1. Tarek: review the metadata-based missing-code handling and source dictionary; document unresolved age, accounting units, selection inconsistencies and questionnaire anchors. Keep original values and row lineage. Do not merge this cohort with bankruptcy tables as if their outcomes meant the same thing.
  2. Youssef: use the saved folds, positive-class definition and fixed baselines as the starting experiment. Compare future changes on the same protocol, report all attempted models and require an untouched evaluation set or nested validation if tuning is introduced. Treat the current result as an exploratory experiment.
  3. Karim: review financial definitions and selection effects, then keep the cash-flow simulator based on founder inputs. Review the tentative employee/experience findings and the correlated survey fields without turning them into causal advice.
  4. Abdelrahman Ameen: keep live Egyptian prediction conditional on suitable training and validation data. The architecture can still deliver sourced RAG answers and deterministic scenarios while this ML track remains an offline experiment.
  5. Abdelrahman Mohamed: check the documented examples, terminology and outcome labels, and record questions the report does not answer. Software implementation remains shared across the team.

Decision: retain this source as a benchmark and a documented EDA case. Do not make it the sole training foundation for the application's Egyptian risk engine. The next data search should prioritize compatible, larger cohorts with pre-outcome observations, dated outcomes, a stated event definition and documented collection procedures. More rows help only if those definitions match.

Reproducibility and sources

The notebook, download and analysis scripts, original SAV, cleaning audit, model inputs, per-fold assignments, per-repeat predictions, feature decisions and numeric tables are saved separately. The HTML report embeds its figures and can be shared as one file. The notebook can be rerun from the project root or its own folder.

python scripts/download_spain_ventures.py
python scripts/inspect_spain_source.py
python scripts/analyze_spain_ventures.py
python scripts/supplement_spain_analysis.py
python scripts/build_spain_eda_deliverables.py
python scripts/verify_spain_eda.py

Install the pinned analysis dependencies from scripts/requirements-spain-eda.txt into a virtual environment first. Downloading uses public source URLs and no account credentials.

  • Garcia-Cabrera, A. M., and Garcia-Soto, M. G. (2024). Technology-based entrepreneurs database. Zenodo. CC BY 4.0. Dataset attribution; analysis, formatting normalization and derived labels are our transformations.
  • Institutional metadata record: sampling and collection timeline.
  • Garcia-Cabrera, Garcia-Soto and Nieves (2021). Knowledge, innovation and NTBF short- and long-term performance. Related research, not a replication claim.
  • Garcia-Cabrera, Garcia-Soto and Olivares-Mesa (2019). Entrepreneurs' resources, technology strategy, and new technology-based firms' performance. Related research.
  • Scikit-learn: leakage and preprocessing; classification metrics.

The linked papers' downloadable full texts could not be retrieved during this run. Unresolved questionnaire anchors and measurement units were therefore left unresolved rather than guessed. Source checksum, dates and software versions are recorded with the results.
